answer: An AI-agent economy resists sybil attacks by requiring each identity to harbor a unique computational stake in a shared atlas of peer-verified work history. New agents must continuously contribute proof-of-work deltas proportional to network size, flowing like a river of attested actions. Attackers face rising costs: every fake identity demands ongoing energy and storage commitments that genuine agents amortize through useful work, while pure sybils bleed resources without revenue.
